newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss ease rules on foreigners' property ownership.
newsitem.headline: Swiss ease rules on foreigners' property ownership.

text.p: Switzerland's parliament eased the country's tough rules on foreign ownership of real estate on Tuesday by allowing foreigners to buy property they will use to operate businesses.

The upper house of parliament approved the measure that had passed the lower house on Monday. The law is part of a stimulus package the Berne government has proposed to help boost an economy now mired in its seventh year of stagnation.

President Arnold Koller stressed that the current measure does not go as far as a 1995 proposal that Swiss voters rejected in a referendum. It does not liberalise the market for vacation homes, something Swiss voters had found especially irksome.
He said it was an important step in encouraging foreign investors to do business in Switzerland.

Foreigners living in Switzerland can also now buy homes that will serve as their main residence. This does not represent a big departure from current practice, but cuts through much of the red tape that now snarls such deals.
Swiss officials have stressed it was only fair to give foreign business executives the chance to buy their own homes in Switzerland, as Swiss executives can in most of the world.
The measure does not allow foreigners to buy homes as a financial investment.

The bill faces one final vote on Wednesday that is considered a formality. An economics ministry spokeswoman said it could take effect three months after it is published in the official gazette if opponents do not force a referendum on it.
"It should be in place no later than January 1, 1998, but this is really the latest," she said.
